title: Золотые руки и острый нож  (Golden Hands and a Sharp Knife)

segments.t: Elena finishes introducing her cooks Kanat and Nadya at Arcobaleno while Misha piles orders onto Viktor, and at Claude Monet Max warns Kostya to stay clear of Denis's knife. Let's listen to the scene in Russian first.
А это Канат, он у нас киргиз.
Никак не может себе сделать гражданство.
Это Надя. Настоящий профессионал.
Руки просто золотые.
За этими золотыми руками иногда нужен глаз да глаз.
Минестроне, сёмга на пару, карпаччо.
Карпаччо, Виктор Петрович.
Да, шеф!
Вот ведь лентяй усатый.
Поговаривают, он алкоголик.
Да по нему и видно сразу.
Осторожней, он моего брата порезал.
Time to unpack every phrase from the exchange you just heard.
А это Канат, он у нас киргиз.
'And this is Kanat, he is our Kyrgyz cook.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'.
Никак не может себе сделать гражданство.
'He just cannot manage to get his citizenship.' Notice how Russian puts 'in no way' and 'citizenship' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
Это Надя. Настоящий профессионал.
'This is Nadya. A true professional.' Here Elena anchors the thought on 'true' and finishes on 'professional', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Руки просто золотые.
'Her hands are simply golden.' In everyday Russian, 'hands' flows straight into 'golden' without extra linking words.
За этими золотыми руками иногда нужен глаз да глаз.
'Though you have to keep a very close eye on those golden hands.' Elena pairs 'golden, gold' with 'of eyes' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
Минестроне, сёмга на пару, карпаччо.
'Minestrone, steamed salmon, carpaccio.' Notice how Russian puts 'minestrone' and 'carpaccio' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
Карпаччо, Виктор Петрович.
'The carpaccio is yours, Viktor Petrovich.' Elena centers this short reply on 'carpaccio', letting a few direct words carry the whole meaning.
Да, шеф!
'Yes, Chef!' Spoken Russian keeps this brief and expressive, built right around 'chef' without extra helper words.
Вот ведь лентяй усатый.
'What a mustachioed slacker.' Chef Barinov pairs 'slacker, idler, lazy person' with 'slacker' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
Поговаривают, он алкоголик.
'People say he is an alcoholic.' Notice how Russian puts 'to people' and 'alcoholic' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.
Да по нему и видно сразу.
'You can tell right away just by looking at him.' Here Elena anchors the thought on 'one can see' and finishes on 'immediately', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Осторожней, он моего брата порезал.

'Be careful, Denis just cut my brother.' In everyday Russian, 'careful, more carefully' flows straight into 'to cut, slice' without extra linking words. Now let's replay the complete scene in Russian without interruption.
